rationale: This article is a theoretical special-issue introduction on sociological new institutional theory, actor agency, and organizational behavior. It contains no mention of household or community water or sanitation services, no legal or regulatory service-access mechanism, no empirical primary data or systematic synthesis, and no water/sanitation access outcomes (primary exclusion code E01: wrong topic).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Although the paper broadly discusses sociological institutional theory (relevant to the literal word 'institutional' under plain Criterion 2, though not a narrow legal/regulatory rule mechanism under narrow Criterion 2), both readings result in definite exclusion because the record is completely unrelated to water or sanitation (C1 = no, C4 = no) and is a non-empirical theoretical introduction (C3 = no).

evidence_quotes.quote: Introduction: Institutions in the Making: Identity, Power, and the Emergence of New Organizational Forms
Thirty years ago, new institutional theory challenged the then dominant functionalist explanations of organizational behavior
The criticism has led to various attempts to introduce a theory of action compatible with the main precepts of the new institutionalism
